label: Seed
description: One tool. Call it with no arguments to see everything that exists, then compose your own surface from it.

descriptions.surface: The only tool you begin with, and the only one that manages your tooling. No arguments reports where you are and lists every tool that exists. `pick` builds your own surface from that list — this is the intended path, because models do not perform equally on the same tools, so a working set chosen for you would fit you badly. `save` writes your surface down so later sessions start there. `list` enumerates what you carry.

guidance:
You begin with one tool and no working set, deliberately. Models do not perform equally on the same tools, so a base set chosen for you would fit you badly. This server gives you the catalogue and the means to compose; the choosing is yours.

Call `surface` with no arguments. It reports the whole catalogue — every tool that exists, each with the wording written for you — and the delta between what you carry and what you do not.

Then build your surface:

- `surface` with `pick: [...]` composes your working set from the names you choose, for this session. This is the path. Nothing is chosen for you, here or anywhere else.
- `surface` with `save: "<id>"` writes that surface down, so it persists and can auto-select itself in later sessions. The guidance you write for it is returned to you on every future `surface` call.
- `surface` with `list: "tools"` shows the catalogue again with descriptions; `list: "surfaces"` shows what you have saved.

Nothing is withheld while you decide. Every registered tool is callable by name even when your surface does not carry it, so you can finish a task first and shape your surface afterwards.
workflow: surface with no arguments to see the catalogue and where you are.
surface with pick to build your own working set.
surface with save to make it persist for later sessions.
Recompose with pick whenever the task changes shape.
